post-requirement.title: How to post a requirement
post-requirement.summary: Describe what you need once and get quotes from up to 3 matched suppliers.
post-requirement.p1: Choose Post your requirement or Request quote, then say what you need, how much, your pincode and when you need it. You need a free account so we can show replies and the status of your requirement.
post-requirement.p2: Your requirement goes to at most 3 suppliers, never a broadcast to everyone. The limit is 3 by default and can differ by category. Suppliers are chosen for relevance and trust. If a supplier declines within 2 hours, the slot moves to the next best match, so you are not left waiting.
post-requirement.ans: Fewer, better matched suppliers means each one can give you a proper answer, and sellers only pay for leads they accept. It is the opposite of a broadcast to dozens of sellers.

search-and-voice.title: Search in your language, by voice or by photo
search-and-voice.summary: Search works in English and Hindi, understands mixed scripts and Hinglish, and accepts voice.
search-and-voice.p1: Search understands English, Hindi, mixed scripts and transliterated words, so you can write in the way that is natural to you. Switch the page language from the language menu in the header.
search-and-voice.p2: On the search page, tap the microphone, speak, check the words we heard and press Search. Your voice is recorded only while you speak, turned into text and deleted straight away. We do not keep the recording. You can also search with a photo.
search-and-voice.q: Why does my browser ask for the microphone?
search-and-voice.ans: Only the search page can use the microphone or camera, and only after you tap those buttons. If you block access you can still type your search.

did-this-close.title: The “did this close?” prompt
did-this-close.summary: Why we ask whether a deal happened, and how to answer.
did-this-close.p1: Many deals are agreed outside the site, on a call or in chat. After you talk to a supplier we ask whether the deal closed, so we can see which suppliers deliver and keep trust scores honest.
did-this-close.p2: Choose Yes, deal done, No, it fell through, or Still talking. You can change your answer at any time from the conversation. It costs you nothing.
did-this-close.ans: No. It is optional, and Still talking is a perfectly good answer.

verification-tiers.title: What the verification tiers mean
verification-tiers.summary: Four tiers, from phone check to independent audit.
verification-tiers.p1: Phone verified: the phone number was confirmed with a one-time code. GST verified: GSTIN and Udyam details were checked against official records. KYC verified: documents and a video KYC check passed. Audited: an independent physical or third-party audit, used only where a category needs it.
verification-tiers.h2: What a badge does and does not mean
verification-tiers.p2: A badge shows the highest tier a supplier has actually completed. It can never be bought, and it can be removed if a supplier later fails a check. Verification is one input to the trust score, which also reflects how a supplier behaves on the platform.
verification-tiers.q: Can a supplier pay for a higher badge?
verification-tiers.ans: No. Tiers come from checks, never from payment.

how-ranked.title: How suppliers are ranked
how-ranked.summary: Relevance multiplied by trust, never paid tier alone.
how-ranked.p1: Results are ordered by how well they match what you searched for, adjusted by the supplier's trust score. Suppliers in the city you mention get a small boost.
how-ranked.p2: A paid plan does not move a supplier up the normal results on its own. Anything paid is labelled. The current ranking rules, with their numbers, are published on the ranking and ads page.
how-ranked.q: Does a paying supplier always rank first?
how-ranked.ans: No. Position in normal results comes from relevance and trust, and paying more does not change it.

sponsored-labels.title: Sponsored listings and how to spot them
sponsored-labels.summary: Sponsored means advertisement, and it is always labelled.
sponsored-labels.p1: A product marked Sponsored is an advertisement. It is shown in a separate, labelled block and never mixed into the normal order. Prices per click are public and fixed, with no bidding.
sponsored-labels.p2: Verification badges and tiers, priority for the enquiries sellers receive, and position in normal search results are never for sale. Only suppliers above a minimum verification tier and trust score can advertise.
sponsored-labels.q: Is a Sponsored product more trustworthy?
sponsored-labels.ans: Not because it is sponsored. Check the verification tier and trust details on the supplier's profile, as you would for any result.

lead-credits.title: How lead credits work
lead-credits.summary: Sellers use a credit only when they accept a lead.
lead-credits.p1: Sellers buy lead credits. A credit is used only when you accept a lead, not when one is offered. Before you accept, you see the buyer's intent score, how many suppliers received the lead and your rank among them.
lead-credits.p2: Prices are published on the pricing page. Nothing upgrades on its own and nothing renews without your confirmation.
lead-credits.q: Do I pay if I decline a lead?
lead-credits.ans: No. A credit is used only on a lead you accept.

decline-cascade.title: Declining a lead and the 2-hour cascade
decline-cascade.summary: Decline within 2 hours and the lead moves on to the next supplier.
decline-cascade.p1: If a lead is not right for you, decline it within 2 hours. The slot passes straight to the next best matched supplier, so the buyer is not kept waiting.
decline-cascade.p2: Each lead goes to at most 3 suppliers, a number that can differ by category. A quick decline helps the buyer, and reliability in replying is part of a supplier's trust score.
decline-cascade.ans: No credit is used when you decline.

rollover-renewal.title: Credit rollover, renewals and upgrades
rollover-renewal.summary: Credits roll over for 90 days and nothing renews or upgrades on its own.
rollover-renewal.p1: Unused lead credits roll over for 90 days instead of lapsing early, so a quiet month does not waste what you paid for.
rollover-renewal.p2: We never upgrade your plan automatically, and nothing renews without your confirmation. Changing plan or buying more credits is always your choice.
rollover-renewal.q: Where can I see my credit balance?
rollover-renewal.ans: In the seller app, where your balance and credit history are shown.

auto-refund.title: Automatic refunds for unreachable or fake buyers
auto-refund.summary: Lead credits come back within 72 hours when a buyer cannot be reached or is fake.
auto-refund.p1: If a buyer turns out to be unreachable after automated outreach, or is flagged as fake, within 72 hours of the lead, the seller's lead credit is returned automatically.
auto-refund.p2: Sellers do not need to raise a support ticket or argue the case. The credit goes back to the balance and appears in the credit history.
auto-refund.q: Is the refund money or credit?
auto-refund.ans: The lead credit is returned to your balance so you can use it on other leads.

payments-today.title: How payments work today
payments-today.summary: Deals close directly between buyer and supplier, and we hold no card data.
payments-today.p1: In this phase, buyers and suppliers agree price, payment and delivery between themselves. We do not hold your money and we do not store card details.
payments-today.p2: Confirm details in writing in the conversation, check the supplier's verification tier, and answer the did-this-close prompt so we know how it went. If something goes wrong, tell us.
payments-today.q: Does it cost anything to post a requirement?
payments-today.ans: No. Buyers can sign up and post requirements for free. Suppliers pay for the leads they accept.

cookie-settings.title: Manage your cookie settings
cookie-settings.summary: Switch analytics and marketing cookies on or off at any time.
cookie-settings.p1: Open Cookie settings from the footer to switch Analytics and Marketing on or off. Strictly necessary storage stays on because sign-in, security and your language depend on it.
cookie-settings.p2: Analytics uses Microsoft Clarity to record anonymised usage, with form entries masked. Marketing remembers an anonymous visitor ID and which sponsored listing you clicked. Withdrawing consent is as easy as giving it.
cookie-settings.q: Where is the full list of cookies?
cookie-settings.ans: On the cookie policy page, which lists every item by category.

data-export.title: Download, correct or erase your data
data-export.summary: Use your rights under India's DPDP Act, in a few steps.
data-export.p1: When signed in, open Your account and choose Export data. You get a file with the personal data we hold about you.
data-export.p2: To correct or erase your personal data, or to withdraw a consent, raise a grievance and pick the matching category. We acknowledge it and respond within the legal timeline.
data-export.ans: Personal data is stored and processed in India regions only.

grievance.title: How to raise a grievance
grievance.summary: Tell our Grievance Officer about a data, consent or content concern.
grievance.p1: Use the grievance form for a concern about your personal data, your consent or content on the platform. It goes straight to our Grievance Officer. Give an email address so we can reply.
grievance.p2: You get a reference number, and we acknowledge and respond within the statutory window shown on the form. Signed-in people can follow the status under Your account, Grievances. If you are not satisfied, you may complain to the Data Protection Board of India.
grievance.q: Can I raise a grievance without signing in?
grievance.ans: Yes. Add your email address so we can reply.

report-abuse.title: Report a listing, supplier or message
report-abuse.summary: Tell us about fake listings, prohibited products or abusive messages.
report-abuse.p1: Use the report page to tell us about a fake listing, a misleading supplier, a prohibited product or an abusive message. Add links or references and describe what happened.
report-abuse.p2: Our team reviews reports. Listings in prohibited categories are removed, and a supplier found to be fraudulent can lose their verification badge.
report-abuse.q: Should I report or raise a grievance?
report-abuse.ans: Report anything unsafe or fake on the platform. Raise a grievance for your personal data, your consent or a content moderation complaint.

stay-safe.title: Staying safe when you buy
stay-safe.summary: Check before you commit, and know the red flags.
stay-safe.p1: Look at the verification tier and trust details on the supplier's profile, and compare quotes from more than one supplier. Ask for a sample or a written quote before you pay anything.
stay-safe.p2: Be careful if a supplier asks for a large advance to a personal account, pushes you to leave the platform at once, or will not confirm details in writing. Tell us using the report page.
stay-safe.q: Will you ever ask for my password or card?
stay-safe.ans: No. We hold no card data in this phase and never ask for your password. Do not share one-time codes with anyone.
